newsitem.title: LATVIA: BALTICS-SUSPENSIONS, SUMMER AND SCARCE NEWS HIT BOURSES.
newsitem.headline: BALTICS-SUSPENSIONS, SUMMER AND SCARCE NEWS HIT BOURSES.

text.p: Baltic bourses sagged this week as suspensions in Vilnius, a lack of big news in Riga and the onset of summer in Tallinn hit the region's struggling markets.
Analysts say the markets in all three countries need bigger companies and more liquidity to break out of their slumps and really roll.
VILNIUS
Official list: ends week at 909.56 versus 922.15
Dealers said that Vilnius remained in the grip of a long, painful correction this week.
It was laid low by the suspension of trade in several key companies because of shareholders' meetings and other business.
Vilniaus Bank, Lithuanian Energy and Sanitas were among the suspensions.
Trading fell into a deep rut on Tuesday, when only 192,000 litas worth of shares were traded on the central market.
One exasperated broker described it as "probably the most terrible day" of the year.
RIGA
Rietumu index: ends week at 181.24 versus 187.29
Riga had posted modest gains throughout the week in generally light trade only to see them wiped out on Friday when the Rietumu index fell 5.98 percent to 181.24.
Friday's market was dragged down by Daugavpils Chain, which fell to 1.17 lats from 2.15 lats as it went ex-bonus.
Dealers said the earlier gains showed that low prices were luring some investors back to the bourse but there was no market moving news to push prices and volumes up significantly.
TALLINN
Talse: ends week at 251.48 versus 252.15

The onset of summer was cited by dealers as one of the reasons for the market's relatively sluggish performance although analysts say it needs to diversify its corporate offerings if it wants steady long-term growth.
The Talse fell in the first half of the week but firmed toward the end of the week as some investor interest revived.
